subject: Order form redlines: IP ownership, training license, and evidence checklist
messages:
From: Miranda Cho <miranda@heliox.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Legal <legal@heliox.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Mar 2029 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines to order form — IP & training questions

Hi Mateo / Laura,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Our legal team sent back a marked-up order form + MSA extract (attached). The two items they pulled for immediate attention are: output ownership and training/data-use — they want clearer carveouts for:

- Customer-generated outputs used in Heliox products (they want assignment vs. license clarified).
- Explicit prohibition on using customer data to further train Redwood models unless Heliox opts in per order form.
- A feedback license scope: we need to ensure aggregated telemetry used to improve infra is permitted, but anything that could deanonymize or recreate Heliox IP is excluded.

Attached: Heliox_MSA_redlines_v2.pdf and OrderForm_Heliox_v1.xlsx. Can you confirm the product/legal positions that Redwood can take here? We need a short list of proposed redline responses and an evidence checklist we can hand to procurement (SOC2 report, telemetry retention policy, KMS certs).

Can we get a one-pager by end of day Wednesday so our procurement can circulate internally? I put Legal on cc — they may add nitty-gritty language.

Appreciate it,
Miranda
Miranda Cho
Head of Product Ops, Heliox Systems

Subject: Re: Redlines to order form — IP & training questions

Hi Miranda — thanks for the flagged items and the attachments. Quick answer up front: Redwood can accept a narrow, opt-in training prohibition and provide a clear feedback license for telemetry, but we need operational controls and customer evidence to do so without major impact to model safety or cost.

Proposed next steps (high level):
1) I’ll draft proposed language for the order form: two short clauses — (A) "Output ownership: customer retains title to customer-provided content and customer-generated outputs; Redwood grants a limited license back to operate the service" and (B) "Training: Redwood will not use customer raw data to train models unless customer checks the opt-in box on the order form and signs Exhibit A (Training Consent)."
2) Suggest an evidence package: SOC 2 Type II link, telemetry retention policy, KMS/HSM attestation, and a short operations note on how prefix/KV caches are isolated. I’ll base that off the Evidence_Checklist_Template.
3) Ben — can you confirm if Dedicated customers with reserved capacity need different language? If we must guarantee no cross-customer model updates, we should document the runtime isolation and mention Dedicated pools + private deployments as separate controls.

I’ll circulate language by EOD Wednesday. If legal wants exact phrasing, looping Laura will help get that signed off.

Best,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Mateo / Miranda — quick operational notes from procurement / sales perspective:

- Dedicated vs Hosted: For Dedicated customers we can represent "no training on customer data" as a contractual control plus runtime isolation in our docs. For Hosted customers we can provide the opt-in checkbox route. Both approaches are acceptable but have different sales/price implications.
- Feedback license: we can offer a bounded, anonymized feedback license (non-reversible aggregates, no PII reconstruction) that allows infra improvements but not model retraining on Heliox-provided data.
- Evidence: procurement will want the SOC2 link, a short one-page runtime isolation statement (I can draft), and a telemetry redaction summary.

Action items: 
- Mateo: please share the draft clauses ASAP so I can map to pricing tiers and check if we need an SLA exception for telemetry retention.
- Laura: can you review the draft and call out any legallandmines?

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Director, Solutions & Procurement

Miranda — looping in legal ops context and delivering the one-pager.

Thanks for the summary. I reviewed Mateo's proposed approach and Ben's operational notes. Attached is a short redline recommendation and an "Evidence Bundle" checklist we will provide to procurement. Key clarifications added: 

- Output ownership: retained by customer; Redwood receives a non-exclusive service license to reproduce outputs solely to deliver the service and run troubleshooting. No assignment of customer downstream product titles.
- Training prohibition: we propose the opt-in Exhibit A model. Exhibit A will require explicit checkbox and a separate signature for training consent; we also add a configurable expiration (12 months) and revocation pathway.
- Feedback license: limited to aggregated service telemetry and performance metrics; we will include an explicit carveout for security telemetry required to remediate incidents. No retention beyond X days without customer consent.

Please see attached: "Heliox_Redline_Responses_v1.pdf" (I exported the redline as a PDF and included the checklist). Ben — the SLA exception for telemetry retention: please scope how many days of retention is market-acceptable; we currently default to 90 days for hosted telemetry but can carve to 180 with pricing adjustments.

Miranda — if that addresses the asks, I can send the tracked redline back to your legal with suggested wording and a link to the Evidence Bundle in HubSpot.

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal & Policy, Redwood Inference
